en:
...Pitch black.
My head hurts.
...What happened to me?
Now I remember!
Someone hit me from behind.
And I passed out... Where am I?
I can't move.
My hands and feet seem to be tied.{p}

Too bright!
The lights suddenly came on, and the glare was so blinding that I shut my eyes.{p}

...When I slowly opened my eyes, I was in the familiar newspaper club room.
I was tied hand and foot with rough rope to the club's big table.
And standing in front of me were seven people, boys and girls.
Faces I recognized.
It was Shindo and the others.
And in the middle of them...
"Yo, {a}. Finally awake, huh?"
Hino was standing there.
He was the newspaper club senior who had set up this meeting and gathered the seven members.
"Hino!"
"What's with the surprised face? That's a real dumb-looking mug you've got there.{p}

Hyahhahha!"
When Hino laughed, the other six laughed too.
Shindo spoke up.
"Yeah, {a}. The seventh member was Lord Hino himself.
No matter who told the stories, whoever told the sixth one was going to take you to the library.
Then we'd knock you out there and start our revenge. That was the plan."
Revenge...?
What revenge?{p}

More importantly, why were Arai and the others here?
Didn't Arai jump off the school roof★
Arai was grinning.
"Oh? {a}.
Does it puzzle you that we're here, when we were supposed to have vanished?
Surely you don't actually believe I jumped off the roof?
Of course I didn't.
You see, you were frightened.
Iwashita, the first to tell a story, ended up like that and went home.
Then Kazama, who told the second story, suddenly vanished too.
...That took root deep in your subconscious and planted a fear that anyone who told a story would surely disappear.
Back then, you tried to save me when I was about to jump, didn't you?
I didn't actually jump.
I only dropped my school uniform jacket.
But that one instant must have tricked you into believing I had jumped.
And then you thought I'd vanished in midair.
It happens, medically speaking.
People convincing themselves an illusion is real, I mean.
And meanwhile, the three of us were making preparations.
Preparations for our revenge on you. Kihihihihi..."{p}

More importantly, why were Iwashita and Kazama here?
Kazama looked at my face and cackled.
"What's wrong, {a}? Is there something on my face?
Did you really think I'd disappeared?
With everyone's help, fooling your eyes was a piece of cake.
Iwashita and I disappeared early, see, so we could start preparing our revenge on you.
Ahahaha."{p}

But what shocked me first of all was that Iwashita was there.
Iwashita, who was supposed to have gone home, was right there.
Iwashita was looking at me with a delighted smile.
"Is there something on my face?
I only pretended to go home, you see. I was getting ready to take my revenge on you."{p}

"...Revenge★"
Except for Hino, I had never met any of them before today.
I couldn't think of anything I'd done to deserve revenge.
I had no idea what they were talking about.
Would anyone really go to such elaborate lengths just to get revenge on me?
"H-Hino. Please, stop joking around.
Don't tell me this is the seventh story of the seven wonders or something?
Please stop, my heart can't take any more.
I'll write a really interesting article, I promise.
Please untie these ropes. They really hurt."
I forced myself to laugh as cheerfully as I could.{p}

But the moment I did, the smiles vanished from Hino's and the others' faces.
"You still haven't figured it out?
This meeting was held for you.
We don't give a damn about any article. The newspaper club was never going to run a feature like that.
All those stories Iwashita and Shindo and the rest told you were made up.
And you sat there listening so earnestly without noticing. You really are a blissful idiot.
This meeting isn't for some feature on the school's seven wonders. It's a special trial, held to take our revenge on you."
Everyone had a serious look on their face.
Wasn't this a joke?
Were they seriously going to put me on trial★{p}

"I will now pronounce the verdict!"
Hino raised his right hand.
And then...
"Death penalty☆"
"No objection!"
"No objection!"
"No objection!"
All of them clenched their right fists, stuck out their thumbs, and jabbed them hard toward the floor.
The end.
"Stop joking around!"
I thrashed.
The rope binding my hands was almost loose...!
"Bring me the item."
Hino solemnly received something from Iwashita.
What was it?
Something very small.{p}

The six jurors and the judge closed in around the table I was tied to.
Every one of them wore a triumphant smile.
A fresh chill ran through me.
This was no joke.{p}

Hino slipped something hard into my barely open mouth.
What...?
A capsule...?
Mmgh!
...I swallowed it.
Once they saw my throat bob as I swallowed, Hino and the others looked very satisfied.
"What you just swallowed is poison.
...Now, now, don't look so shocked.
You won't die right away. It's in a capsule.
But once your stomach acid dissolves the capsule and the poison inside gets out, that's it for you.
Nothing left to do but die.
...Let's see. By my calculations, you've got about five hours left before you die, I'd say."
Hino looked very pleased with himself.
"...Y-you're joking, right?"
I'm sure my voice sounded pathetic.
I would surely have done anything at all, if only they would tell me it was a joke.{p}

"I'm happy to say it's no joke.
How does it feel to have only five hours left?
Got the shivers? Breaking out in a cold sweat?
Uhihihihi...
This is fun, {a}.
But if you just gave up now, it wouldn't be any fun for us at all.
We need you to live as hard as you can right up until you die.
So I've prepared this."{p}
From his pocket, Hino took out a small glass vial filled with a yellow liquid.{p}"It's an ampoule of antidote. Drink this in time, and it'll neutralize the poison in the capsule. Want it?"
I want it!
I don't need it!

"I want it!"
"'I want it'? That's not how you ask, is it? 'Could I please have it, Lord Hino?' Go on, say that."{p}Hino waved the ampoule spitefully right in front of my eyes.
Could I please have it, Lord Hino?
I'll never say that, not even if it kills me

"...C-could I please have it, Lord Hino?"
They looked at one another and laughed.
...Screw them!
Why should I have to go through this!{p}

"Hyahhahha. Good, good, that's a good kid. People should do as they're told, right?
If you want it that badly, lick my shoe."
With that, Hino planted his dirty shoe next to my head.
The humiliation...!{p}But if I defy him...
Lick the shoe
No matter what, I can't do that

...There's no other way.
If I don't lick it, I won't survive.
I shut my eyes, swallowed my tears, and licked his shoe.
"Wahahahaha! This guy's actually licking my shoe! Disgusting!
...Look at that, the guy's crying."
...For now, I have to endure whatever they say.
There's nothing I can do but endure.{p}

"I know! Let's all get our shoes licked. That's the way to do it.
Otherwise it wouldn't be fair."
Kazama, damn him.
...Just you wait.{p}

Hino was clapping his hands with glee.
"Kazama, ni-i-ice idea! Come on, {a}. Lick everyone's shoes.{p}Do that, and I'll give you the ampoule."
Lick everyone's shoes
There's no way I can do that

...I licked everyone's shoes, just as I was told.
When I had finished licking every one of them, I looked at Hino.{p}

"Aaaaaaaaah☆"
No matter how loudly I screamed, the ampoule fell slowly, hit the floor and shattered.
The ampoule broke, and the liquid inside splattered all over the floor.
"That's not what you promised!"
I shouted.
If my hands had been free, I would have grabbed him.
Even so, Hino wasn't the least bit flustered and stayed perfectly calm.
"Relax. I'll keep my promise.
I've hidden one exactly like that ampoule somewhere in this school.
The time limit is five hours.
...Oops, only four and a half left now. Find it before then."
...These people!{p}

These guys... what kind of people are they?!
They want to have fun watching me search like mad★
"I'll untie you now.
Listen, just because you're free, don't you lay a hand on us.
If you try anything against us, I'll smash that ampoule.
I'm the only one who knows where it's hidden.
And one more thing. Don't you dare leave the school.
If you so much as try to leave the school, I won't hesitate to get rid of the ampoule.
Even if you go to the police or a hospital, nobody's going to take your story seriously.
There's only one way you can be saved.
Find the ampoule hidden somewhere in this school.
There's only one rule to keep.
Don't leave the school.{p}

Our revenge has begun.
Now, I'll untie you!"
Iwashita and the others untied my ropes.
My hands and feet were free at last.
I glared at Hino as hard as I could.
But Hino was laughing.
"Whoa. Wanna hit me? Go ahead, hit me.
Then I'll smash the ampoule.{p}What'll it be, {a}?"
Hit him
Hold back for now

"Hurry!"
"Hurry!"
"Hurry or you'll die!"
They all jeered at me together.
...I wanted to beat the hell out of them, but I didn't even have the time to spare for that.
For now, just like they said, finding the antidote came first.{p}
"Hurry, hurry, {a}! If you don't hurry, you're gonna diiiiie!"{p}
Hosoda, the fatso, pretended to run, huffing and puffing.{p}

Watching them only made me angrier.
I ran out of the newspaper club room.{p}

The cheers seeing me off stabbed into my back.
Shut up.
I felt like a marathon runner heading out of the stadium.
I looked at the watch Hino had given me.
It was digital.
It read eleven o'clock at night.
I set the watch's stopwatch.{p}

Four hours and thirty minutes left.
Now, hurry!{p}Where should I go first?
Chemistry lab
Art room
Nurse's office
Gym
Old school building
Faculty room
Night-duty room
Other
Classroom
Restroom
School gate
Flower beds
Home ec room
Newspaper club room
Library
Other

...The faculty room!
If I don't go to the faculty room first, I won't get in anywhere.
...Come to think of it, what happened to the teacher on night duty?
I'd better make sure I don't get caught.{p}

I reached the faculty room.
...Thank goodness.
Luckily, the faculty room was unlocked.
The lights were off, too.
I slipped into the faculty room.{p}

There was no time.
I couldn't afford to take it slow.{p}What should I do?
Search the cabinets
Search the desks
Search the bulletin board
Make a phone call
Go somewhere else

A phone!
There's a phone right here!
I can just call for help.
If I call someone, anyone, they're sure to come and help me.{p}Who should I call?
My home
The police
The fire department
The hospital
My homeroom teacher's house
Dial at random
Those bastards even cut the phone line!{p}Anyway, I'll Search elsewhere.

I went through every cabinet in the faculty room, one after another.
But all they held were documents.
Nothing like a small ampoule vial in there.
...Think carefully.
Where would they hide it?
Where could they have put it?
But the more I thought about it, the more it seemed they could have hidden it anywhere.
In the end, there was nothing worth noting in the cabinets.{p}Where should I search?

I went through every last desk in the faculty room.
With dozens of teachers, just searching all the desks took me a good while.
I only searched them roughly, and I didn't find anything worth mentioning.{p}Should I search them more carefully?
I decided to search the desks one more time.{p}

...Here it is!
...No, it wasn't.
It was an energy drink.
Who leaves something this misleading in their desk?!
...Huh?
What's this, a screwdriver set?
No, wait.
It might come in handy.
I'll take the screwdrivers.
I slipped the little screwdriver set into my pocket.
Still no ampoule.
Time was just slipping uselessly away.{p}What now?

There couldn't be anything on the bulletin board... A bunch of keys!
Of course!
So this is where the keys were hanging.
Without these keys, I can't get in anywhere that matters.
At this hour, most of the rooms are locked.
I absolutely have to take these with me.{p}

I helped myself to the bunch of keys hanging on the bulletin board.
There was nothing else of use on the board.{p}What now?
I'll try somewhere else.{p}
Where should I go next?
I decided to head for the chemistry lab.{p}
I decided to unlock the door with the bunch of keys I'd brought from the faculty room.{p}
Now, where should I search?
Search the chemical shelves
Search the tables
Search the cupboard
Go to the chemistry prep room
Make a phone call
Go somewhere else

I searched the chemical shelves.
Row after row of bottles held chemicals I'd never even seen before.
They all looked alike, and every single one of them looked like it could be the one.{p}...Should I just try drinking them all?
Drink them
Don't drink them

No, this stuff could be the real poison.
If I drank some strange chemical and something happened that couldn't be undone, I'd be in serious trouble.
Remember the shape of that ampoule.
What I'm looking for has to look exactly like that ampoule.{p}I'll Search elsewhere.

The chemistry lab had eight large tables.
They were fairly easy to search.
I searched all eight tables from top to bottom.
But there was nothing worth mentioning in them.{p}It can't be helped.
I'll Search elsewhere.

I searched the cupboard.
It was full of papers I'd never seen before.
There were a number of reports written by students.
One of them caught my eye.
It was a research report by Reiko Fukuzawa.
It was titled "Trends in Human Life and Death Over One Hundred Days."{p}...I don't have much time, but should I read it?
Read it
No need to read it

...I turned the page.
What follows is the text of the report she wrote.{p}

For this experiment, I chose one man.
My grandpa.
Grandpa is going to die soon.
He doesn't have any symptoms he's aware of yet, but that's what the doctor said.
Apparently he won't last another hundred days.
So I decided to write a report on the last hundred days of Grandpa's life.{p}

Day 1.
After dinner, Grandpa coughed up a little blood.
This has been going on for a long time now.
Other than that, he was the same as always.{p}

Day 3.
After dinner, we had a family meeting.
It was to discuss whether or not to put Grandpa in the hospital.
Mom was crying that keeping him at home and looking after him was too hard on her.
I thought this was my chance and said I would look after him, but Dad said, "You have school, don't you?" and he was against it.
I cried.
Fake crying, of course.
Maybe because that worked, Grandpa got to stay at home.
Now I can keep going with my research.
From behind the sliding door, I watched Mom sigh once she was alone.{p}

............Day 46.
Starting today, Grandpa's medicine changed.
I'm sure that's poison.
Mom must be worn out from looking after him, so she decided to kill Grandpa by giving him poison.
I plan to find a chance and check it soon.{p}

Day 47.
From this day on, Grandpa could barely even walk.
It must be because of yesterday's poison.
I think Grandpa is coughing up more blood than before, too.{p}

Day 48.
Grandpa's convulsions wouldn't stop, so the doctor came.
The doctor gave him three really fat injections.
The doctor recommended that it was about time he went into the hospital.
I tried desperately to stop it.
Even so, it looks like he can't stay home much longer.
My fake crying didn't work this time.
But summer vacation is coming soon, and then I'll have free time, so it's fine if he goes into the hospital.{p}

Day 49.
Grandpa seems to have started realizing that he's going to die.
Until then he still had a little energy left, but suddenly it was all gone.
Is that just the kind of creature human beings are?
Somehow, it's no fun.
I want him to try harder to live.{p}

Day 50.
I went up to Grandpa and
asked him, just to see,
"Grandpa, are you going to die?"
Of course he's going to die.
Then Grandpa smiled weakly without saying a word and stroked my head with his skeletal hand.
This person knows that he's going to die.
He still has to live fifty more days for me, and like this, it's no fun.
I've started to wonder whether I should change my research subject.
Maybe that would be better.
I want things that are going to die to struggle desperately right up to the end.{p}

This report covers the first fifty days.
I'd like to hand in the remaining fifty days once they're complete.{p}

That was the end of the report.
...What kind of girl does that?!
And she had the nerve to hand this in as a school report.
I checked the submission date. It was three days ago.
Change her research subject?
Don't tell me she means me?
You've got to be kidding me!
Before I knew it, I had crushed the report in my fist.
This report might be useful for something.
I decided to take it with me.{p}All right, I'll Search elsewhere.
I decided to go to the chemistry prep room next to the chemistry lab.{p}
Where should I search?
Search the cupboard
Search the desk
Go back to the chemistry lab
I decided to go back to the chemistry lab.{p}
What now?

I decided to go to the art room.
I couldn't imagine that ampoule being kept in the art room... but maybe a place like that is exactly where it would be.{p}
The art room was locked.{p}
I unlocked it with the bunch of keys I'd brought from the faculty room.{p}
What now?
Search the shelves
Search the tables
Search the tool shelf
Go to the art prep room
Go somewhere else

I searched the shelves.
They held all sorts of books about art.
There was nothing that looked like an ampoule.
Where should I search?{p}

Suddenly, a person's shadow was reflected in the glass of the shelf.
Someone was behind me.{p}What now?
Should I turn around?
Or should I pretend I haven't noticed and keep searching the shelves a little longer?
Turn around
Pretend not to notice

I pretended to keep searching the shelves a little longer.
The shadow reflected in the glass crept closer and closer to me.
It stopped right behind me.
And then it raised its arm.
...Now!
I slammed my shoulder into whoever it was.{p}

"Gyah!"
Caught off guard, my attacker took the full force of my tackle and went down.{p}

I threw myself on top of my attacker.
It was Kazama.
"You bastard!"
I wrapped my hands around Kazama's throat and squeezed.
Kazama let out a strangled groan.
"Ch... choking... Let go of me. I'm gonna die here, you know?"{p}What now?
Choke him even harder
Loosen my grip a little

I didn't hold back. I choked him even harder.
"Don't screw with me! I'm the one who's about to die here!"
"S-stop... gweh!
I-if you do this, Hino and the others won't let it slide... you know..."{p}

A wood plane dropped from Kazama's hand.
Don't tell me he was going to attack me from behind with that?{p}
Even as I choked him, Kazama still wore a faint smirk.
Punch him
Choke him even harder
Slam his head into the cabinet
Let him go

There was no reason to hold back with him anymore.
Still choking him, I rammed Kazama's face into the cabinet.{p}

"Gyah!"
The glass shattered with a tremendous crash, and I shoved Kazama's head right through it.
Maybe he had cut his head on the glass; a single line of blood was trickling down Kazama's forehead.
"...I'll kill you."
I said it right into Kazama's ear.
"F... forgive me! I-I'm sorry!"
At once, Kazama turned into a different person and begged me for forgiveness.
...When I begged them to forgive me, these bastards just laughed.
And yet now, this guy had done a complete about-face and turned meek.
"I-I'll do anything, so please, forgive me.
P-please, I'm begging you!"
"You'll do anything? Really?"
I pressed him.{p}

"Y-yes!"
Kazama nodded hard, again and again.
Every time he nodded, blood ran down from his head.{p}What now?
Punch him
Ask why he's trying to kill me
Ask where the ampoule is
Let him get away
Tie him up

That seemed to get on Kazama's nerves.
Suddenly, he glared at me and turned defiant.
"Forgot? You're saying you forgot? You might forget, but I won't.
Do you remember a rainy day two months ago?"
"Like I'd remember something like that!"
"That day, I had a date.
And you went through a puddle and splashed water all over me.
My pants got dirty.
The pants I was wearing for the very first time that day, and you got them dirty!
And you didn't even apologize!
My date was ruined!
So I won't be satisfied until I kill you☆"
Eyes bloodshot, Kazama lunged at me.{p}
I sent him flying with a punch and pinned him down again.{p}

...I was so appalled I couldn't say a word.
He really tried to kill me for a reason like that?
Just because some water splashed on his pants?
And it wasn't even on purpose. It was just an accident.
On top of that, I don't even remember whether it ever happened.
And yet he held a grudge over it and tried to kill me?
...Is this guy out of his mind?
A fresh wave of terror washed over me.
Do I really have to die for people like them?{p}

"Go on, kill me! Why don't you just kill me! Ptui!"
Kazama spat at me.{p}What should I do?
Maybe what I'd said earlier had set him off. Kazama showed no sign of dropping his defiant attitude.{p}What should I do?
Punch him
Get tough with him
Apologize and get him to calm down

"...How'd you like to die?"
I was going to die soon.
I was going to die, all because of scum like them.
Why should I have to apologize to a guy like this?
"You told me to kill you a minute ago. Want me to kill you, just like you asked?
Even if you die, there are plenty of other ways to find the ampoule."
I tried to slam Kazama's head into the cabinet again.
This time into the other cabinet, the one with its glass still intact...
"...Stop! I'm sorry! I'll tell you anything!"
Kazama shrieked, his voice cracking.
"You should've said that from the start. Where's the ampoule?"
"...Th-that's something only Hino knows."
"You want to die?"
"It's true! It really is! I really don't know!"
It looked like he truly didn't know.
...If I believed what he said, my only options were to search for the ampoule or to ask Hino directly.
There was no point in going after any of the others.{p}What should I do?

I yanked the cord out of an electric drill in the art room and tied Kazama up with it.
Then I tried to stuff a rag into his mouth.{p}

"Stop! That's filthy! What are you doing to my beautiful face?!"
"Shut up! Be grateful I'm not killing you!"
I shoved the dirty rag into Kazama's mouth.
He mumbled and struggled, but he soon gave up and went quiet.{p}
Right. Time to make my move.

I searched the tool shelves.
There was no ampoule.
But there were plenty of saws, hammers and the like.
"...Looks like I'm going to end up fighting them."
I rummaged through the tool shelves.
I wanted to take the whole toolbox, but it looked heavy and would only get in my way.
From it, I picked out a hammer and a saw.{p}

Two-sword style.
I felt like Miyamoto Musashi.
This really was a matter of life or death.
I jammed the hammer and the saw into my belt.{p}Now, what should I do?
I headed for the art prep room next to the art room.{p}
What should I do?
Search the cabinets
Search the desk
Go back to the art room
I decided to check the cabinets.{p}

The cabinets were full of paintings, apparently done by art club students.
Of course the ampoule wouldn't be in a place like this.{p}

...Huh?
Among them, I found a portrait.
"It's Iwashita."
I had no idea who had painted it, but the person on that canvas was unmistakably Akemi Iwashita.
"This might come in handy."
I decided to take the painting with me.{p}What should I do next?
I went back to the art room.{p}What should I do?
I decided to go to the old school building.{p}

...The old school building.
Even in the state I was in, the old school building still scared me.
There was no electricity in the old school building, so unless I had a flashlight, there was no way I could search it.
I didn't have a flashlight.{p}What should I do?
Should I go inside the old school building anyway?
Go in
Go somewhere else

All the same, I went into the pitch-dark old school building.
...It was no use.
There was no way I could even tell left from right.
...I'd better give up.{p}
Where should I go?

That's it!
There should be a teacher on duty in the night-duty room!
I didn't know which teacher it was, but I'd go and see.
If I explained what was going on, maybe something could be done?
...No, would I just get yelled at?
It was all or nothing. I'd go and see!{p}
The door was locked.{p}

What should I do?
Should I try to get in?
Or should I go somewhere else?
Unlock the door
Go somewhere else
I opened the door with the bunch of keys I'd brought from the faculty room.{p}
The TV was on.{p}The teacher was watching it, back turned to me.
Run over to the teacher
Take a good look around the room

Something was wrong.
The teacher was right there inside, yet didn't answer?
...Could something have happened?
Without thinking, I looked around the room.
There was nowhere in this room for anyone to hide.
I called out once more.
"...Teacher?"
But still no answer came back.
I ran over and put my hand on the teacher's shoulder.
And then...
The teacher slumped limply over.
"Aaagh!"
The teacher's throat had been slit wide open, straight across.{p}

I turned around to see Shindo lunging at me from the doorway.
He had a knife in his hand.
"Whoa!"
I dodged it by a hair.
The knife grazed my cheek.
It burned!
I pulled the hammer and the saw out of my belt.{p}

Seeing that, Shindo grinned.
"Packing some pretty dangerous stuff there, huh?
You planning to take me on with that?"
Shindo held his knife ready, watching me closely.
He looked like he was well used to fighting.
If I charged in carelessly, I'd be the one who got taken down.
But the same went for Shindo.
We each watched the other, waiting.{p}

"Did you kill the teacher?"
"Yeah. They were in my way."
This guy... he kills a person and doesn't feel a thing?
If this kept up, time would just keep slipping away.{p}
What should I do?
Rush in close to him
Throw the hammer at him
Apologize
Run away for now

"Guhh!"
I quickly snatched up the knife he had dropped and pressed it against his throat.
Shindo was trembling.
Then he went still.
Was he waiting for me to slip up, or had he given up?{p}
What should I do?
Press the knife in harder
Ask why he's trying to kill me
Ask where the ampoule is
Let him go
Tie him up

"Where's the ampoule?"
"Beats me."
I pressed the blade against him.
"Lie to me and I'll kill you. I don't have much time left.
I don't mind killing you and taking you down with me."
Cold sweat beaded on his forehead.
"...I really don't know. Only Hino knows."{p}
...So what Kazama said was true after all.{p}

"Why are you trying to kill me? I've never done anything to deserve your revenge!"
At that, Shindo's eyes flew wide open, then he gave me a look of contempt and snorted.
"...Hmph. You say you don't know me?
Figures, for a lowlife like you.
I bet you don't even remember the time I was out recruiting new students for my club."
I frowned.
Club recruitment...
I'd talked with plenty of upperclassmen, but I didn't remember Shindo's face.
"That look says you don't remember.
Not that I expected you to.
I called out to you again and again.
But you ignored me and just walked off."
"And?"

Then he glared at me and bit his lip in frustration.
Blood dripped from the lip he bit so hard.
"...Because you're not even worth killing."
"Just watch! I'll curse you!
I'll curse you to death!"
Hino yanked the screwdriver out of his shoulder and stabbed it into his own ear.
"Gyah!"
Hino let out a short groan.
Then Hino's eyes rolled back until only the whites showed.
"...I...'ll... c...urse... y...ou... t...o... d......e...a...th......"
He fell.
It wasn't as if I couldn't have foreseen Hino taking his own life.
But I wasn't able to stop him.
I had no time to stop him, and even if I had, would I have stopped Hino?
"...If you want to curse me, go ahead. I'm not afraid of your curse.
Thanks to you, I've got the confidence to live strong."
No answer to my words came back from Hino.
By now, he must be riding the train to hell.{p}

I stepped into the phone booth outside the school gate.
The morning sun was already starting to show at the far edge of the sky.{p}

I dialed.
"...Hello, police? There's been a murder at the school. The school is at........."{p}

I told them everything and hung up.
I was unnaturally sleepy.
It was hard to stay awake any longer.
I crumpled to the floor of the phone booth.
...Even keeping my eyes open was hard now.
I closed my eyes.
And I sank into a deep sleep.
When I wake up, maybe I'll skip school, just for today.
...As my consciousness faded, the wail of police sirens echoed through my head.{p}
Where should I go?

The knife is gone!
I must have dropped it somewhere.{p}
